skill.displayName: Work Productivity Skillscan Security Workflow Helper

llm.summary: This is a documentation-style workflow helper with no executable code, credentials, persistence, or hidden data access, though its activation wording is broader than ideal.

dimensions.detail: The skill asks for local-friendly scripts, templates, checklists, small-model or CPU-safe workflows and does not request broad filesystem, network, credential, or profile access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown instructions, a reference document, and a small OpenAI agent manifest; no executable install scripts, package managers, or setup commands were present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions are disclosed and mostly coherent, but the description and trigger keywords include broad terms such as security, every, must, pass, and before, which could cause unintended implicit invocation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, background worker, privilege escalation, credential handling, session use, or automatic mutation behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact's purpose is to help users build checklists, plans, templates, analysis, and local-friendly workflows for SkillScan-style security workflow tasks, and its capabilities are limited to agent guidance.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, be aware that this skill may be selected too often for generic security or productivity requests because its trigger language is broad and implicit invocation is enabled. It appears safe as a workflow helper, but users or maintainers should narrow its trigger terms if precise skill routing matters.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] unexpected: The scanner's overbroad-invocation concern is supported by the artifact: broad trigger words and allow_implicit_invocation are present. I downgrade this to a scoping and routing note rather than Review because the artifact has no executable code, hidden behavior, sensitive data access, privileged authority, persistence, or destructive capability.
